newsitem.title: UK: Season ticket holders win in Newcastle share race.
newsitem.headline: Season ticket holders win in Newcastle share race.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Newcastle United said on Monday that season ticket holders who had applied for shares in the club's flotation would be allocated approximately 500 stg worth of stock each.
The Retail Offer has been increased from 10 percent to approximately 15 percent of the total placing to help meet demand from fans of the north-east England club.
The club said that no shares would be allocated to members of the public who are not season ticket holders at Newcastle's St James Park stadium.

Season ticket holders will get 370 shares in the club. Newcastle announced on Friday that the offer price had been set at 135p, the top of the indicative price range, valuing the club at 193 million stg.
Newcastle said the Retail Offer was seven times oversubscribed. It said interest in the Institutional Offer "significantly" exceeded the amout of the Offer.

"We are particularly pleased to have enabled our season ticket holders to become shareholders in the company. However, we regret that demand has meant that we were unable to satisfy applications from the general public." said Newcastle United Plc chairman Sir Terence Harrison.
"The flotation has established a strong base for us to move forward and everyone in the business will be working hard to achieve future success," he added.
